findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the `finding_type` (`DEFECT` default / `HARDENING`) field: where it is set in Phase 2, that it is carried on the Phase-2->3 survivor gate, and that the Phase-3 Remediation Plan item schema (remediation.md ll. 49-51) records it so approval.md can flag it.
evidence: Plan: `harm_reachable == "no"` additionally **reclassifies** the finding from `DEFECT` to `HARDENING`
Plan Edit 3: 'flag any item reclassified as HARDENING' at approval time
grep of examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/ for HARDENING and DEFECT both return zero matches — no finding_type axis exists today
remediation.md lines 49-51 Remediation Plan schema lists `provenance`, `impact`, `finding_refs`, `cascade_flag`, `effort` — no finding_type/HARDENING field, and Edit 2's scope does not add one
Phase-2->3 gate (verification.md line 204) carries 'validity, impact, citations, why_it_matters' — not a finding_type
findings.finding: The plan introduces a DEFECT->HARDENING reclassification and requires approval.md to flag HARDENING items, but no finding_type/DEFECT/HARDENING axis exists in the skill today and Edit 2 does not thread the label through Phase 3's plan-item schema — leaving the HARDENING flag no defined data path from Phase 2 to Phase 4.
findings.location: Edit 1 (verification.md reclassification note) and Edit 2 (remediation.md), vs. Edit 3 (approval.md HARDENING flag)
scenarios: A finding scores harm_reachable=no, survives the floors, gets a remediation move in Phase 3, but the Phase-3 plan item carries no HARDENING label, so Phase 4 cannot flag it as hardening — the exact 'hardening presented as a bug' outcome the plan promises to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `finding_type` to the Phase-2 survivor payload and to the remediation.md per-item schema in Edit 2's scope, defaulting to DEFECT and set to HARDENING on harm_reachable==no, so the label the reclassification note creates has an explicit path to the approval flag.

evidence: grep confirms neither 'DEFECT' nor 'HARDENING' currently exists anywhere under examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/ — this is a new enum introduced by the plan

findings.location: Edit 1 (verification.md HARDENING reclassification) and Edit 2 (remediation.md Remediation Plan item) and Edit 3 (approval.md)

Design text uses '-0.10' throughout: '**-0.10 validity penalty**', 'takes the -0.10 at Phase 2'
Verify-command taxonomy (1)/(6): prose-vs-pattern literal mismatch
findings.finding: The acceptance criterion greps for the literal string 'minus 0.10', but every occurrence of the penalty in the plan's design text is written as '-0.10' (e.g. '**-0.10 validity penalty**', 'takes the -0.10 at Phase 2'). Unless Edit 1 is written to literally emit the phrase 'minus 0.10', this proving command fails on an otherwise-correct artifact.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — third checkbox; Edit 1 penalty prose
scenarios: Author writes the scoring bullet as '... minus a 0.10 penalty ...' using '-0.10' and the grep for 'minus 0.10' returns no match, failing the AC despite correct content.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the AC to `grep -nE '[-−]0\.10' ...verification.md` (anchored to the numeric form the design actually uses), or commit Edit 1 to literally contain 'minus 0.10'.

`grep -n 'prior-decision' SKILL.md`

A reader/verifier must reconcile three tokens for one concept, and each grep depends on that file using its specific spelling.

findings.finding: The prior_decision AC uses `grep -c -E 'explicit_justified|explicit_bare|incidental|prior_decision' ... returning >= 4`, which counts matching LINES across a broad alternation and does not prove all four distinct emitted values are present — `prior_decision` alone appearing on 4+ lines satisfies it while `incidental` or `explicit_bare` could be missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with four separate matches, e.g. `grep -n 'explicit_justified' ...`, `grep -n 'explicit_bare' ...`, `grep -n 'incidental' ...`, and the existing `grep -n '| \`none\` |' ...` row all matching.

findings.finding: The prior_decision concept is spelled three different ways across the acceptance criteria and files: 'prior_decision' (verification), 'prior decision' (approval AC6), and 'prior-decision' (SKILL.md AC7).
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one canonical token (e.g. `prior_decision`) for the identifier and, if SKILL.md prose uses a hyphenated/spaced display form, note that intentional variance in the AC so the greps match the text as actually written.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State (in Edit 2's rationale) that asymmetric proposers make convergence rarer by design and confirm the divergence research round is expected to run for most survivors — or justify why convergence is still expected to be common.
evidence: Plan: proposers now 'answer **different questions on different evidence**' (A=OSS practice, B=this project's record)
Plan: 'The move-level convergence judge is retained unchanged (`same_approach` OR `same_end_state`)'
Plan: 'What is replaced is the *tiebreak*' — framed as an exception path
Two proposers answering different questions on different evidence will far less often produce the same_approach/same_end_state match than two reading identical evidence did
findings.finding: By making the two proposers answer structurally different questions on different evidence while keeping the same_approach/same_end_state convergence judge unchanged, cross-proposer convergence becomes rare by construction, so the 'divergence research round' — described as a tiebreak — becomes the default path for most survivors rather than an exception; the plan does not acknowledge this cost/frequency shift.
findings.location: Edit 2 — remediation.md asymmetric proposers + divergence research round
scenarios: Most survivors no longer converge, so nearly every survivor triggers a per-survivor research round put to both records — turning the 'targeted' tiebreak into the common per-run cost, and pushing many items to `no-consensus` (user-decides) that previously auto-resolved.

findings.finding: `prior_decision`'s four-value enum is closed over records-found-or-absent, but the four backing queries (`git log -S`, `git blame -L`, ADR/docs grep, ticket-id grep) can fail to run (no/shallow git history, absent ADR or ticket store) rather than return an empty record. The plan specifies no fallback distinguishing 'query unavailable' from `none` ('queries returned no record'), so the verifier's classification is undefined when a query cannot execute.
findings.location: Edit 1 — verification.md `prior_decision` query block and four-value table
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line to the `prior_decision` section: a query that cannot execute contributes no record (treated as `none` for that query); classify `explicit_*`/`incidental` only from queries that actually ran, and never apply the -0.10 penalty on a classification derived solely from unavailable queries.

findings.finding: AC2's prose claims the file documents 'all four emitted values' but its grep pattern tests only three of them, omitting 'none'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fourth anchored check for the 'none' value, e.g. grep -nE '`none`' ...verification.md, or word-anchor it within the prior_decision block so it is not a substring false-positive on the common word 'none'.

findings.finding: The -0.10 prior_decision validity penalty has a cross-phase ordering defect: it is applied during Phase-2 scoring, but its exemption condition ('the remediation names what evidence has changed since', via the Phase-3 `evidence_changed` field) is only knowable in Phase 3 — after the Phase-2 floors have already dropped or kept the finding.
findings.location: Edit 1 (verification.md prior_decision penalty) and Edit 2 (remediation.md evidence_changed)
findings.suggested_fix: State that the Phase-2 penalty is provisional: the verifier records `prior_decision == explicit_justified` and the -0.10 is held, but the floor decision for such findings is deferred to a Phase-3 re-score once the move's `evidence_changed` field is known (or, equivalently, the penalty is applied only to findings that reach Phase 3 without an `evidence_changed` move).

findings.finding: The -0.10 `explicit_justified` validity penalty is defined in Phase-2 verification.md but its trigger ('only when the finding's remediation does not name what evidence has changed since') depends on the Phase-3 `evidence_changed` field, which Edit 2 places on the Phase-3 Remediation Plan item — an artifact that does not exist when Phase-2 computes validity. The rule is not co-located with the schema/phase that owns the field it scores, and it is ambiguous whether the penalty scores the finding's Phase-2 remediation *direction* or the Phase-3 move's `evidence_changed` field.
findings.location: Edit 1 (verification.md scoring bullet, `prior_decision` penalty) and Edit 2 (remediation.md `evidence_changed`)
findings.suggested_fix: Score the penalty against the finding's Phase-2 *remediation direction* (already carried into Phase 2 per verification.md lines 18-20): the direction must name the changed evidence to avoid the -0.10. Keep Phase-3 `evidence_changed` as the plan-item mirror of the same claim, and state explicitly in verification.md that the penalty reads the Phase-2 direction, not the not-yet-existing Phase-3 field.

findings.finding: The -0.10 validity penalty's trigger references a field that does not exist at the point the penalty is applied. The penalty is applied during Phase-2 deterministic scoring, but its condition — 'the remediation does not name what evidence has changed' — refers to a Phase-3 remediation, which is not produced until after Phase-2 scoring and floors run. Phase 2 findings carry only a 'suggested remediation direction,' not a Phase-3 remediation move with an evidence-change justification field.
findings.location: Approach item 1 (the -0.10 penalty); verification.md scoring (lines 71-79) vs. remediation.md 'What each proposer returns' (lines 7-12)
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the penalty to the Phase-2 finding record: apply -0.10 when `prior_decision == explicit_justified` AND the finding's own why_it_matters / suggested-direction text does not name what has changed since the recorded decision.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the arbitration/precedence rule for combining the four `prior_decision` queries into a single value (e.g. any source showing recorded reasoning => explicit_justified; else any showing a deliberate choice => explicit_bare; else incidental if state is traced but undecided; else none).
evidence: Edit 1: 'classifies what they return into exactly four values, with the record's content deciding'
Four queries can return divergent signals; no stated precedence among explicit_justified/explicit_bare/incidental/none when sources disagree
E2 signal (2): implicit classification protocol
findings.finding: The `prior_decision` check runs four heterogeneous deterministic queries (git log -S, git blame -L, ADR/docs grep, ticket-id grep) and must collapse their combined output into exactly one of four values, but the plan does not specify how conflicting query results arbitrate (e.g. git log shows a bare choice while the ADR grep shows recorded reasoning, or one query returns a record and others return nothing). 'with the record's content deciding' names the tiebreak dimension but not the resolution rule.
scenarios: A symbol has a bare commit trailer (explicit_bare) but an ADR that later justifies it (explicit_justified) — two verifiers reading the same records could classify differently, undermining the -0.10 penalty determinism.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a precedence sentence to Edit 1: classify by strongest signal across all four queries — reasoning-present => explicit_justified; deliberate-choice-without-reasoning => explicit_bare; traced-but-undecided => incidental; no record => none.
